newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended higher, the long end strengthening after U.S. markets rebounded following an initial drop on release of the U.S. producer price index.
The December PPI rose by a strong 0.5 percent in the overall number, but by only 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. U.S. nonfarm payrolls are due on Friday IZYX.

"People are very positive about the numbers tomorrow," one Swiss-based trader said. Traders saw strong demand late in the day for longer-dated cash Confederate bonds after the U.S. PPI. March Conf bond futures face next major resistance at 116.35, near the contract high of 116.37 set December 20.
One trader who said gains were led by futures believed the market may be due for a correction. "Optically, it looks expensive," he said. But short rates may stay low for a while.
The weak Swiss economy has made it unlikely that the Swiss National Bank will tighten anytime soon.

Swiss data released Thursday showed the jobless rate at a post-war high of 5.3 percent. Expectations the economy will stay weak for the foreseeable future have made any tightening now appear highly unlikely, and some economists believe the Swiss National Bank might even ease further, although the discount rate at 1.00 percent matches historic lows.
Germany's December jobless rate was also up at 10.8 percent and the numbers of jobless hit a post-war record as well.
In the Swiss domestic market, traders said utility firm Atel's 12-year Swiss franc bond set Monday met good demand.
Dec Comi medium-term bond up five at 111.05
Mar Euro Swiss francs down one at 98.16.
